```
void UShallowWaterSubsystem::RegisterImpact(FVector ImpactPosition, FVector ImpactVelocity, float ImpactRadius)
{
	if (ShallowWaterNiagaraSimulation == nullptr)
	{
		return;
	}
	
	FHitResult OutHit;
	GetWorld()->LineTraceSingleByChannel(OutHit, ImpactPosition + FVector(0,0,10.f), ImpactPosition + FVector(0,0,-10.f),
		GetImpactCollisionChannel());
	AWaterBody* WaterBody = Cast<AWaterBody>(OutHit.GetActor());
	if (WaterBody == nullptr)
	{
		return;
	}
	Tracker_Directs.Add(FShallowWaterCollisionTracker_Direct(GetWorld()->GetTimeSeconds(), GSWImpactTrackerActiveForSeconds, WaterBody));
	
	if (!ShallowWaterNiagaraSimulation->IsActive())
	{
		// queue up impacts we missed
		PendingImpact TmpImpact;
		TmpImpact.ImpactPosition = ImpactPosition;
		TmpImpact.ImpactVelocity = ImpactVelocity;
		TmpImpact.ImpactRadius = ImpactRadius;
		PendingImpacts.Add(TmpImpact);

		return;
	}

	WriteImpactToNDC(ImpactPosition, ImpactVelocity, ImpactRadius);
}

// these impacts are a frame or two late, and we only want to update the Niagara system and not 
// perform an additional overlap test
void UShallowWaterSubsystem::FlushPendingImpacts()
{
	for (PendingImpact CurrPendingImpact : PendingImpacts)
	{
		WriteImpactToNDC(CurrPendingImpact.ImpactPosition, CurrPendingImpact.ImpactVelocity, CurrPendingImpact.ImpactRadius);
	}
	PendingImpacts.Reset();
}

void UShallowWaterSubsystem::WriteImpactToNDC(FVector ImpactPosition, FVector ImpactVelocity, float ImpactRadius)
{
	FNiagaraDataChannelSearchParameters SearchParams(ImpactPosition);
	const UNiagaraDataChannelAsset* NDC = Settings->DefaultShallowWaterCollisionNDC.Get();
	if (NDC == nullptr)
	{
		return;
	}
	
	if (UNiagaraDataChannelWriter* DCWriter = UNiagaraDataChannelLibrary::WriteToNiagaraDataChannel(ShallowWaterNiagaraSimulation, NDC, SearchParams, 1, false, true, true, TEXT("ShallowWaterWriteImpact")))
	{
		int32 Index = 0;
		DCWriter->WritePosition(TEXT("Position"), Index, ImpactPosition);
		DCWriter->WriteVector(TEXT("Velocity"), Index, ImpactVelocity);
		DCWriter->WriteFloat(TEXT("Radius"), Index, ImpactRadius);
	}
}

void UShallowWaterSubsystem::SetWaterBodyMIDParameters(AWaterBody* WaterBody)
{
```

```
UBasicShallowWaterSubsystem::UBasicShallowWaterSubsystem()
{

bool UBasicShallowWaterSubsystem::ShouldCreateSubsystem(UObject* Outer) const
{
	TObjectPtr<UShallowWaterSettings> TmpSettings = GetMutableDefault<UShallowWaterSettings>();
	if (TmpSettings && !TmpSettings->UseDefaultShallowWaterSubsystem)
	{
		return false;
	}
	else
	{
		return Super::ShouldCreateSubsystem(Outer);
	}	
}

bool UBasicShallowWaterSubsystem::IsShallowWaterAllowedToInitialize() const
{
	TObjectPtr<UShallowWaterSettings> TmpSettings = GetMutableDefault<UShallowWaterSettings>();
	if (TmpSettings)
	{
		return TmpSettings->UseDefaultShallowWaterSubsystem;
	}

	return false;
```
```
}

int32 UGeometryCollectionComponent::GetInitialLevel(int32 ItemIndex)
{
	using FGeometryCollectionPtr = const TSharedPtr<FGeometryCollection, ESPMode::ThreadSafe>; 

	int32 Level = INDEX_NONE;
	if (RestCollection && RestCollection->GetGeometryCollection())
	{
		const TManagedArray<int32>& Parent = RestCollection->GetGeometryCollection()->Parent;
		int32 TransformIndex = INDEX_NONE;

		FGeometryCollectionItemIndex GCItemIndex = FGeometryCollectionItemIndex::CreateFromExistingItemIndex(ItemIndex);

		if (GCItemIndex.IsInternalCluster())
		{
			if (const TArray<int32>* Children = PhysicsProxy->FindInternalClusterChildrenTransformIndices_External(GCItemIndex))
			{
				if (!Children->IsEmpty())
				{
					// find the original cluster index from first children
					TransformIndex = Parent[(*Children)[0]];
				}
			}
		}
		else
		{
			TransformIndex = GCItemIndex.GetTransformIndex();
		}
```

```
}

void UDynamicMeshComponent::FinishPhysicsAsyncCook(bool bSuccess, UBodySetup* FinishedBodySetup)
{
	TArray<UBodySetup*> NewQueue;
	NewQueue.Reserve(AsyncBodySetupQueue.Num());

	int32 FoundIdx;
	if (AsyncBodySetupQueue.Find(FinishedBodySetup, FoundIdx))
	{
		// Note: currently no-cook-needed is reported identically to cook failed.
		// Checking AggGeom.ConvexElems & ContainsPhysicsTriMeshData here is a hack to distinguish the no-cook-needed case
		// These checks mirror those from UBodySetup::GetCookInfo.
		// TODO: remove this hack to distinguish the no-cook-needed case when/if that is no longer identical to the cook failed case
		const ECollisionTraceFlag BodyCollisionType = FinishedBodySetup->GetCollisionTraceFlag();
		const bool bEmptySimpleCollision = FinishedBodySetup->AggGeom.ConvexElems.Num() == 0;
		const bool bEmptyComplexCollision = !ContainsPhysicsTriMeshData(false);
		const bool bNoCookNeeded =
			(BodyCollisionType == CTF_UseSimpleAsComplex && bEmptySimpleCollision) ||
			(BodyCollisionType == CTF_UseComplexAsSimple && bEmptyComplexCollision) ||
			(BodyCollisionType == CTF_UseSimpleAndComplex && bEmptySimpleCollision && bEmptyComplexCollision);
		if (bSuccess || bNoCookNeeded)
		{
			// The new body was found in the array meaning it's newer, so use it
			MeshBodySetup = FinishedBodySetup;
			RecreatePhysicsState();

			// remove any async body setups that were requested before this one
			for (int32 AsyncIdx = FoundIdx + 1; AsyncIdx < AsyncBodySetupQueue.Num(); ++AsyncIdx)
			{
				NewQueue.Add(AsyncBodySetupQueue[AsyncIdx]);
			}

			AsyncBodySetupQueue = NewQueue;
		}
		else
		{
			AsyncBodySetupQueue.RemoveAt(FoundIdx);
		}
	}
}
```

```
}

void UShallowWaterSubsystem::UpdateGridMovement()
{
	if (ShallowWaterNiagaraSimulation == nullptr)
	{
		return;
	}
	
	APawn* CursorPawn = GetTheMostRelevantPlayerPawn();
	if (CursorPawn == nullptr)
	{
		return;
	}
	
	const FVector CursorPawnLocation = CursorPawn->GetActorLocation();
	
	/*
	 * Snap the sim center to player character
	 */
	// #note this query gets the closest water surface in 3D space, not a 2D topdown projection as we instinctively assumed
	// Could be better and could be worse

	float BestDistanceSqr = FLT_MAX;
	TOptional<FVector> BestWaterLocation;
	TWeakObjectPtr<AWaterBody> NewBestWaterBody;

	for (TWeakObjectPtr<AWaterBody> WeakWaterBody : LastOverlappingWaterBodies_Internal)
	{
		if (const AWaterBody* WaterBody = WeakWaterBody.Get())
		{
			const TValueOrError<FWaterBodyQueryResult, EWaterBodyQueryError> WaterInfo = WaterBody->GetWaterBodyComponent()->TryQueryWaterInfoClosestToWorldLocation(
				CursorPawnLocation, EWaterBodyQueryFlags::ComputeLocation);

			if (!WaterInfo.HasValue())
			{
				continue;
			}

			const FVector WaterLocation = WaterInfo.GetValue().GetWaterSurfaceLocation();
			const float ds = FVector::DistSquared(WaterLocation, CursorPawnLocation); 
			if (ds < BestDistanceSqr)
			{
				BestDistanceSqr = ds;
				BestWaterLocation = WaterLocation;
				NewBestWaterBody = WeakWaterBody;
			}
		}
	}

	if (!BestWaterLocation.IsSet())
	{
		return;
	}

	// Check to see if the best water body has changed
	bool BestWaterBodyChanged = NewBestWaterBody != BestWaterBody;
	BestWaterBody = NewBestWaterBody;

	const FVector ProjectedLocation = FVector(CursorPawnLocation.X, CursorPawnLocation.Y, 0);
	ShallowWaterNiagaraSimulation->SetWorldLocation(ProjectedLocation);
	ShallowWaterNiagaraSimulation->SetVariableFloat(FName("WaterHeightAtParent"), BestWaterLocation.GetValue().Z);

	// time left before sim is destroyed- used to attenuate waves
	const float SecondsSinceCollision = GetWorld()->GetTimeSeconds() - LastTimeOverlappingAnyWaterBody;
	const float SecondsUntilDestroyed = FMath::Max(0, GSWRemainActiveForSeconds - SecondsSinceCollision);
	ShallowWaterNiagaraSimulation->SetVariableFloat(FName("SecondsUntilDestroyed"), SecondsUntilDestroyed);

	ShallowWaterNiagaraSimulation->SetVariableBool(FName("UseDebugRender"), GSWDebugRender == 1);
	
	if (BestWaterBodyChanged && BestWaterBody != nullptr)
	{
```

### Copilot

**Feasible with native UE runtime components plus custom C++ and authored destruction assets—not as a turnkey assembly of stock editor tools. The ≥60 FPS requirement remains unproven.** The installed engine is **5.8.2**, changelist **56702186**, confirmed in `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Build\Build.version:2–6`.

The strongest architecture is **pre-fractured Chaos buildings + genuinely deformable mesh terrain + bounded WaterAdvanced simulation + Niagara cosmetic debris**. Do not promise fully destructible native Landscape, unrestricted volumetric river physics, or final-game performance from capability inspection alone.

All paths below are relative to `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\`. Inspection was read-only; no editor calls, builds, installations, or mutations occurred.

## 1. Buildings: pre-fracture, explicit supports, selective simulation

**Verified:** Chaos supports pre-fractured Geometry Collections, hierarchical clustering, connection graphs, strain-driven breakage and runtime rigid-body separation. It does not automatically turn a scan into a suitably fractured, structurally meaningful building. ([dev.epicgames.com](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/destruction-overview))

**Recommended implementation**

- Author buildings as foundation, floor, wall-bay and roof clusters, with smaller fracture pieces beneath them. Preserve convincing interior surfaces and wall thickness; use the processed LiDAR geometry as the visual reference, not an assumed structural model.
- Use intact root-proxy rendering before damage; keep nearby destruction assets resident before weapons can hit them.
- Cannon hits should use the struck Geometry Collection’s **`FHitResult.Item`**, localized external strain and bounded breaking velocity—not a newly spawned world-wide field actor per shot.
- Keep persistent gameplay damage separately from transient physics strain. This provides deliberate cumulative cannon damage, save/load and repeatable tests.
- Add a **small authored support graph** connecting structural sections to foundations. Recompute reachability after relevant breaks or terrain-support changes, then release disconnected sections. This is a proposed gameplay layer, not a verified automatic structural-engineering feature.
- Let large released sections collide and drive secondary collapse. Convert small fragments to cosmetic Niagara debris; retain coarse rubble collision and damage state rather than restoring the intact building when physics is culled.

### Installed API evidence

For the following rows, `GC` means  
`Source\Runtime\Experimental\GeometryCollectionEngine\Public\GeometryCollection\`.

| Purpose | Verified API/property | Exact reference |
|---|---|---|
| Local damage | `ApplyExternalStrain(ItemIndex, Location, Radius, PropagationDepth, PropagationFactor, Strain)` | `GC\GeometryCollectionComponent.h:704–714` |
| Internal strain modification | `ApplyInternalStrain(...)` | `GC\GeometryCollectionComponent.h:716–726` |
| Release whole selected cluster | `CrumbleCluster(ItemIndex)` | `GC\GeometryCollectionComponent.h:728–734` |
| Supports | `SetAnchoredByIndex`, `SetAnchoredByBox`, `SetAnchoredByTransformedBox` | `GC\GeometryCollectionComponent.h:743–758` |
| Released-piece motion | `ApplyBreakingLinearVelocity` | `GC\GeometryCollectionComponent.h:766–773` |
| Simulation limits | `EnableClustering`, `MaxClusterLevel`, `MaxSimulatedLevel` | `GC\GeometryCollectionComponent.h:1001–1020` |
| Damage tuning | `SetDamageThreshold`, `SetDamagePropagationData`, collision-damage switch | `GC\GeometryCollectionComponent.h:1029–1058` |
| Debris interaction | `OneWayInteractionLevel`, `SetOneWayInteractionLevel` | `GC\GeometryCollectionComponent.h:982–988` |
| Break notifications | `SetNotifyBreaks`, `OnChaosBreakEvent` | `GC\GeometryCollectionComponent.h:1226–1228,1268–1269` |
| Intact visual proxy / Nanite | `RootProxyData`, `SetEnableNanite` | `GC\GeometryCollectionObject.h:639–654` |
| Cleanup | Remove-on-sleep, sleep time, removal duration, slow-moving threshold | `GC\GeometryCollectionObject.h:792–814` |

Important details:

- The local-strain radius tests **piece centers of mass**, not arbitrary surface intersection. Author sufficiently small wall sections for reliable local holes. `GeometryCollectionComponent.h:704–710`.
- Hit item indices can represent internal clusters. Do not treat them indiscriminately as authored transform indices. The implementation converts them through `FGeometryCollectionItemIndex` at `Source\Runtime\Experimental\GeometryCollectionEngine\Private\GeometryCollection\GeometryCollectionComponent.cpp:6826–6840,6919–6946`.
- Runtime anchoring APIs exist in this build; older guidance implying all anchors must be established only during construction is incomplete.
- Root proxies improve rendering, **not automatically physics residency**. Explicitly budget both.

For bombs, use a bounded target query followed by per-component damage, or a short-lived radial field where necessary:

- `UFieldSystemComponent::ApplyStrainField` and `ApplyPhysicsField`:  
  `Source\Runtime\Experimental\FieldSystem\Source\FieldSystemEngine\Public\Field\FieldSystemComponent.h:168–205`.
- Construction versus persistent fields and removal: same file, `212–270`.
- `URadialFalloff::SetRadialFalloff`: sibling `FieldSystemObjects.h:402–409`.
- External/internal strain and velocity targets:  
  `Source\Runtime\Experimental\Chaos\Public\Field\FieldSystemTypes.h:150–158`.

Keep the configurable “TNT yield” as an **explicitly game-only, clamped authored profile**, mapping to gameplay damage, crater shape, visual scale and concurrency limits—not real explosive calculations.

## 2. Terrain: real craters require a different runtime surface

**Verified limitation:** `FLandscapeEditDataInterface`, including `SetHeightData`, is enclosed by `WITH_EDITOR` in:

`Source\Runtime\Landscape\Public\LandscapeEdit.h:34,125–146,586`.

The runtime `RenderHeightmap` node exports height information into a render target; it is not a runtime terrain-sculpting API. ([dev.epicgames.com](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/BlueprintAPI/Landscape/Runtime/RenderHeightmap))

**Recommendation:** make the destructible playable ground a tiled mesh surface from the outset. Use native Landscape only outside that area, or prepare its holes/absence during authoring. **Do not place crater meshes above an unchanged Landscape collider.**

Start with a fixed-topology height-grid per tile:

- Modify actual vertex heights, normals and material attributes.
- Keep shared tile-edge samples authoritative to prevent seams.
- Accumulate crater state with bounded depth and vertex counts.
- Process grid calculations on worker-owned data, then commit component changes on the game thread.
- Queue and coalesce repeated impacts per tile.
- Treat collision completion as part of crater completion, not merely visual completion.

### Native choices

**Preferred: `UDynamicMeshComponent`**

`Source\Runtime\GeometryFramework\Public\Components\DynamicMeshComponent.h` provides:

- `SetMesh`, `EditMesh`: `210–223`.
- `FastNotifyPositionsUpdated`: `284–287`.
- `SetComplexAsSimpleCollisionEnabled`: `716–722`.
- Deferred collision updates: `724–729`.
- `UpdateCollision`: `742–747`.
- `bUseAsyncCooking`: `772–777`.
- Protected virtual `FinishPhysicsAsyncCook`: `836–837`.

The implementation actually performs asynchronous cooking and replaces physics state at  
`Source\Runtime\GeometryFramework\Private\Components\DynamicMeshComponent.cpp:1598–1705`.

**Critical caveat:** asynchronous cooking means rendering and collision are not automatically synchronized. Add a custom generation-aware completion path; reject obsolete results and publish matching visual/collision revisions together. The source also distinguishes “no cook needed” from failure internally—do not interpret its callback boolean alone as universal success.

**Alternative: `UProceduralMeshComponent`**

`Plugins\Runtime\ProceduralMeshComponent\Source\ProceduralMeshComponent\Public\ProceduralMeshComponent.h`:

- Create sections: `189–196`.
- Update sections: `226–233`.
- Collision settings: `274–285`.
- Experimental warning: `144–146`.

**For tunnels/overhangs:** fixed height grids are insufficient. Native mesh boolean subtraction exists through:

- `Source\Runtime\GeometryCore\Public\Operations\MeshBoolean.h:158–186`: `FMeshBoolean`, `Compute()`.
- `Plugins\Runtime\GeometryScripting\Source\GeometryScriptingCore\Public\GeometryScript\MeshBooleanFunctions.h:176–185`: `ApplyMeshBoolean`.

Treat general booleans as a later, separately budgeted feature—not the initial crater path. Validate output topology and failures.

**Rendering limitation:** Epic documents Dynamic Mesh without Nanite, mesh distance fields, automatic LODs or instanced rendering, and documents limitations for Lumen participation. Blueprint Geometry Scripting calls also remain synchronous from the calling game thread. Consequently, keep mutable terrain geographically bounded and explicitly test its lighting beside static city geometry. ([dev.epicgames.com](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/geometry-scripting-users-guide-in-unreal-engine))

## 3. Water: useful native implementation, important flight-specific constraints

**Verified:** this installation includes experimental **WaterAdvanced**, a runtime plugin depending on Water, Niagara and NiagaraFluids:

`Plugins\Experimental\WaterAdvanced\WaterAdvanced.uplugin:13–36`.

Its `UShallowWaterSubsystem` exposes typed `RegisterImpact(FVector, FVector, float)` and water-material integration. This is a genuine native local interaction path, not just a hypothetical shader effect. ([dev.epicgames.com](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/API/Plugins/WaterAdvanced/UShallowWaterSubsystem))

### Implementation and traps

- `RegisterImpact` checks initialization, traces **10 cm above/below the supplied position**, requires hitting an `AWaterBody`, and writes position/velocity/radius into a Niagara Data Channel:  
  `Plugins\Experimental\WaterAdvanced\Source\WaterAdvanced\Private\ShallowWaterSubsystem.cpp:669–727`.
- Therefore, resolve the **water-surface impact position**, not the eventual underwater bomb position; verify the collision channel and readiness before submitting.
- The default subsystem is **disabled by default** through `UseDefaultShallowWaterSubsystem=false`:  
  `...\Public\ShallowWaterSettings.h:49–57`.
- Default simulation parameters are a **2,000 cm grid with 512 maximum-axis resolution**:  
  `...\Public\ShallowWaterCommon.h:13–20`.
- The implementation centers its grid on the relevant pawn’s XY position:  
  `...\Private\ShallowWaterSubsystem.cpp:548–605`.

That last point matters for flight: a distant cannon impact may fall outside the simulated patch. **Do not assume enabling the plugin gives impact-centered simulation across the river.** For the first slice, keep water impacts within a deliberately configured local patch. Larger-range support needs a custom integration or an explicitly cosmetic distant-wave representation.

Water queries should use the current failure-aware API:

`Plugins\Experimental\Water\Source\Runtime\Public\WaterBodyComponent.h:303–309`

- `TryQueryWaterInfoClosestToWorldLocation(...)`
- `GetWaterSurfaceInfoAtLocation(...)`

The older query is deprecated in 5.7. Also, ordinary **River** bodies do not support the standard wave-asset path: `IsWaveSupported()` excludes River in `...\Private\WaterBodyComponent.cpp:156–158`.

**Recommended effect:** local shallow-water disturbance plus a separate Niagara vertical plume, spray, foam and mist. The river simulation should not be expected to produce the entire airborne plume.

**Not established:** volumetric river simulation, automatic bidirectional coupling to newly cratered bathymetry, or accurate physics queries reflecting every transient GPU ripple. The inspected water component explicitly supports **baked** shallow-water data for queries/physics (`WaterBodyComponent.h:437–447`). These broader capabilities must not be promised as stock typed-editor deliverables.

## 4. Niagara and resource control

Use break events to feed a **bounded shared effects stream**, rather than spawning an actor/system per brick. Combine large Chaos fragments with GPU cosmetic chips, dust sheets, material-specific splinters and secondary impact puffs. Prefer baked fluid flipbooks for expensive rolling dust; Epic distinguishes game-oriented 2D fluid templates from cinematic 3D templates and warns that fluid simulations can be costly. ([dev.epicgames.com](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/niagara-fluids-in-unreal-engine))

Verified integration:

| Capability | Installed reference |
|---|---|
| Pooled spawning and pre-culling | `Plugins\FX\Niagara\Source\Niagara\Public\NiagaraFunctionLibrary.h:82–98` |
| Distance, visibility, instance and global-budget controls | `Plugins\FX\Niagara\Source\Niagara\Classes\NiagaraEffectType.h:115–151,154–254` |
| Significance / cull reaction | Same file, `425–438` |
| Data-channel batch writing | `Plugins\FX\Niagara\Source\Niagara\Public\NiagaraDataChannelFunctionLibrary.h:49–50,162–163` |
| Typed position/vector/float writes | Sibling `NiagaraDataChannelAccessor.h:132–162` |
| Optional direct Chaos event interface, thresholds and spatial limits | `Plugins\Experimental\ChaosNiagara\Source\ChaosNiagara\Classes\NiagaraDataInterfaceChaosDestruction.h:358–478` |

Prime pools during loading, assign Effect Types, constrain effect bounds, and avoid giving cosmetic debris gameplay collision. GPU particles still incur system/emitter CPU costs; pooling alone does not remove those costs. ([dev.epicgames.com](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/scalability-and-best-practices-for-niagara))

**Native emergency controls also exist**, but change destruction behavior and need explicit tests:

- `p.Chaos.Clustering.PerAdvanceBreaksAllowed`
- `p.Chaos.Clustering.PerAdvanceBreaksRescheduleLimit`
- `p.Clustering.ParticleReleaseThrottlingMinCount`
- `p.Clustering.ParticleReleaseThrottlingMaxCount`

Exact definitions:  
`Source\Runtime\Experimental\Chaos\Private\Chaos\PBDRigidClustering.cpp:72–76,1656–1662`.

Particle throttling can disable released particles; it is not a transparent “same simulation, faster” switch.

### Proposed starting budgets—not measured capacities

| Resource | First-slice target |
|---|---|
| Concurrent major collapses | 2 |
| Active Chaos fragments | 512 target; 768 hard admission ceiling |
| Mutable terrain | 25 m tiles, 0.5 m sample spacing; ≤16 resident tiles |
| Terrain processing | ≤2 worker jobs; ≤1 collision/mesh publication per frame |
| Water simulation | One 256² patch; increase only after measurement |
| Large plume/dust systems | ≤4; micro-impacts consolidated |
| CPU budget | Game-thread critical path ≤8 ms; Chaos contribution target ≤2 ms |
| GPU budget | ≤13 ms total; Niagara ≤2 ms and water interaction ≤1 ms within that total |

Use distance hysteresis for activation, preserve damage when unloading, and replace settled simulation with coarse rubble representation. Do not remove all useful collision merely to meet the fragment cap.

## 5. Modules and plugins

**Expected direct runtime modules**, depending on chosen includes:

`Core`, `CoreUObject`, `Engine`, `PhysicsCore`, `Chaos`, `ChaosSolverEngine`, `GeometryCollectionEngine`, `FieldSystemEngine`, `GeometryCore`, `GeometryFramework`, `Niagara`, `Water`, `WaterAdvanced`, `GameplayTags`.

Relevant build-rule evidence:

- `Source\Runtime\Experimental\GeometryCollectionEngine\GeometryCollectionEngine.Build.cs:11–41`.
- `Plugins\Experimental\WaterAdvanced\Source\WaterAdvanced\WaterAdvanced.Build.cs:19–40`.

**Enable:** Niagara, Water, WaterAdvanced; WaterAdvanced declares NiagaraFluids as a dependency. Water and WaterAdvanced are marked experimental; NiagaraFluids is beta in the installed descriptors.

**Optional:** ChaosNiagara for its direct data interface; GeometryScripting for Blueprint geometry operations; ProceduralMeshComponent if choosing that terrain implementation.

**Authoring only:** GeometryCollectionPlugin/Fracture/PlanarCut/Dataflow as needed. Do not confuse `ChaosSolverPlugin` with the runtime solver module: its descriptor contains **ChaosSolverEditor**, whereas runtime integration uses `ChaosSolverEngine`.

Stock Blueprint-callable APIs do **not** establish equivalent `ue-editor-control` coverage. Parent must verify typed creation/configuration of fracture assets, Niagara graphs, water settings/materials and runtime classes. No such coverage was inspected here.

## 6. Bounded first slice and acceptance gates

**Recommended slice:** one approximately 150 m city block, two fully destructible three-storey buildings, two contextual buildings, four crater-capable terrain tiles, a river strip, slow flight, cannon and gravity-bomb inputs. All impacts enter one game-owned event path so damage, terrain and effects share an event ID and profile.

| Test | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| Local cannon damage | Selected wall bay fractures; undamaged neighboring bays and buildings remain intact. |
| Support loss | Removing the fixture’s final support starts release within 250 ms; unsupported floor descends rather than floating indefinitely. |
| Real crater | Fixture produces ≥1 m geometric depression; downward collision traces agree with the new surface within 10 cm after completion. |
| Tile seam | Impact across a four-tile corner leaves no geometric or collision crack; neighboring border samples match. |
| Collision readiness | Crater geometry/collision revision is published within 100 ms at the admitted workload; failures are logged and fail the test. |
| Water interaction | Surface impact produces plume and visible outward disturbance; land impact does not. Test both active and initially inactive simulation. |
| Yield configuration | Minimum/maximum profiles remain within all caps; invalid/non-finite values are rejected; no real-world explosive conversion. |
| Persistence | Unload/reload retains broken building sections and crater state. |
| Saturation | Sustained maximum legal firing plus both collapses does not exceed caps, grow queues indefinitely or silently drop gameplay damage. |
| Visual quality | Close, street-level and flight-height captures show convincing interiors, staged collapse, dust/debris separation and water response—not a smoke cloud hiding missing destruction. |

Automation support is installed:

- `AFunctionalTest::AssertTrue`, `FinishTest`, `SetTimeLimit`, preparation/readiness hooks:  
  `Source\Developer\FunctionalTesting\Classes\FunctionalTest.h:415,669–684,773–814`.
- Native simple and latent tests:  
  `Source\Runtime\Core\Public\Misc\AutomationTest.h:4087,4297`.

Use tolerances and outcome assertions for Chaos, not exact fragment-by-fragment deterministic trajectories.

### Performance certification

The **finished packaged game**, not only this slice, must pass on this Windows machine.

1. Record CPU/GPU, driver, RAM/VRAM, build, map, output/internal resolution, upscaler and quality settings. Disable frame generation for the ≥60 FPS proof. Declare the tested visual preset; do not silently reduce it.
2. Use a fixed-seed flight/impact route covering streaming, close-up collapse, overlapping dust, maximum admitted firing, craters and water effects.
3. Separate loading/warmup from gameplay explicitly; run **three 180-second gameplay captures**, retaining every measured frame.
4. Report average FPS, p95/p99/max frame time, CPU/GPU timing and frames over **16.667 ms**. For a literal “never below 60” acceptance interpretation, require **zero measured gameplay frames over 16.667 ms**—average ≥60 or p99 alone is insufficient.
5. Capture a cold first-use run separately to expose loading/PSO hitches, then repeat the final scene with low-overhead measurement to distinguish trace overhead.

Use Unreal Insights channels such as `cpu,gpu,frame,bookmark,loadtime,niagara`, with `-statnamedevents` and a local `-tracefile`; these channels and switches are documented by Epic. ([dev.epicgames.com](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-insights-reference-in-unreal-engine-5))

Instrument damage dispatch, support evaluation, terrain work/publication, collision cooking and effect admission using:

- `TRACE_CPUPROFILER_EVENT_SCOPE`: `Source\Runtime\Core\Public\ProfilingDebugging\CpuProfilerTrace.h:453`.
- `CSV_SCOPED_TIMING_STAT` / custom counters: sibling `CsvProfiler.h:120–155`.
- `FCsvProfiler::BeginCapture` / `EndCapture`: `CsvProfiler.h:519–529`. Await the completion future before declaring the capture persisted.

**Decision:** proceed with this bounded native-runtime architecture, with explicit custom terrain/support/effect coordination. Keep “fully destructible Landscape,” unrestricted physical water and “finished game ≥60 FPS” marked **unsupported or unverified** until their respective implementation and measurement gates are satisfied.

### Copilot

Clean footprint-based shells make the building pipeline more practical, but solid prisms still need floors, wall thickness and support structure for convincing collapse. I’ll check whether the enabled ProceduralMeshComponent can support the first crater slice without adding another geometry stack.

```
void UProceduralMeshComponent::UpdateMeshSection(int32 SectionIndex, const TArray<FVector>& Vertices, const TArray<FVector>& Normals, const TArray<FVector2D>& UV0, const TArray<FVector2D>& UV1, const TArray<FVector2D>& UV2, const TArray<FVector2D>& UV3, const TArray<FColor>& VertexColors, const TArray<FProcMeshTangent>& Tangents)
{
	SCOPE_CYCLE_COUNTER(STAT_ProcMesh_UpdateSectionGT);

	if(SectionIndex < ProcMeshSections.Num())
	{
		FProcMeshSection& Section = ProcMeshSections[SectionIndex];
		const int32 NumVerts = Vertices.Num();
		const int32 PreviousNumVerts = Section.ProcVertexBuffer.Num();

		// See if positions are changing
		const bool bSameVertexCount = PreviousNumVerts == NumVerts;

		// Update bounds, if we are getting new position data
		if (bSameVertexCount)
		{
			Section.SectionLocalBox = Vertices.Num() ? FBox(Vertices) : FBox(EForceInit::ForceInit);

			// Iterate through vertex data, copying in new info
			for (int32 VertIdx = 0; VertIdx < NumVerts; VertIdx++)
			{
				FProcMeshVertex& ModifyVert = Section.ProcVertexBuffer[VertIdx];

				// Position data
				if (Vertices.Num() == NumVerts)
				{
					ModifyVert.Position = Vertices[VertIdx];
				}

				// Normal data
				if (Normals.Num() == NumVerts)
				{
					ModifyVert.Normal = Normals[VertIdx];
				}

				// Tangent data
				if (Tangents.Num() == NumVerts)
				{
					ModifyVert.Tangent = Tangents[VertIdx];
				}

				// UV0 data
				if (UV0.Num() == NumVerts)
				{
					ModifyVert.UV0 = UV0[VertIdx];
				}
				// UV1 data
				if (UV1.Num() == NumVerts)
				{
					ModifyVert.UV1 = UV1[VertIdx];
				}
				// UV2 data
				if (UV2.Num() == NumVerts)
				{
					ModifyVert.UV2 = UV2[VertIdx];
				}
				// UV3 data
				if (UV3.Num() == NumVerts)
				{
					ModifyVert.UV3 = UV3[VertIdx];
				}

				// Color data
				if (VertexColors.Num() == NumVerts)
				{
					ModifyVert.Color = VertexColors[VertIdx];
				}
			}

			// If we have collision enabled on this section, update that too
			if (Section.bEnableCollision)
			{
				TArray<FVector> CollisionPositions;

				// We have one collision mesh for all sections, so need to build array of _all_ positions
				for (const FProcMeshSection& CollisionSection : ProcMeshSections)
				{
					// If section has collision, copy it
					if (CollisionSection.bEnableCollision)
					{
						for (int32 VertIdx = 0; VertIdx < CollisionSection.ProcVertexBuffer.Num(); VertIdx++)
						{
							CollisionPositions.Add(CollisionSection.ProcVertexBuffer[VertIdx].Position);
						}
					}
				}

				// Pass new positions to trimesh
				BodyInstance.UpdateTriMeshVertices(CollisionPositions);
			}

			// If we have a valid proxy and it is not pending recreation
			if (SceneProxy && !IsRenderStateDirty())
			{
				// Create data to update section
				FProcMeshSectionUpdateData* SectionData = new FProcMeshSectionUpdateData;
				SectionData->TargetSection = SectionIndex;
				SectionData->NewVertexBuffer = Section.ProcVertexBuffer;

				// Enqueue command to send to render thread
				FProceduralMeshSceneProxy* ProcMeshSceneProxy = (FProceduralMeshSceneProxy*)SceneProxy;
				ENQUEUE_RENDER_COMMAND(FProcMeshSectionUpdate)
				([ProcMeshSceneProxy, SectionData](FRHICommandListImmediate& RHICmdList) { ProcMeshSceneProxy->UpdateSection_RenderThread(RHICmdList, SectionData); });
			}

			UpdateLocalBounds();		 // Update overall bounds
			MarkRenderTransformDirty();  // Need to send new bounds to render thread
```

```
void FBodyInstance::UpdatePhysicalMaterials()
{
	SCOPE_CYCLE_COUNTER(STAT_UpdatePhysMats);
	UPhysicalMaterial* SimplePhysMat = GetSimplePhysicalMaterial();
	TArray<FPhysicalMaterialMaskParams> ComplexPhysMatMasks;
	TArray<UPhysicalMaterial*> ComplexPhysMats = GetComplexPhysicalMaterials(ComplexPhysMatMasks);

	FPhysicsCommand::ExecuteWrite(GetPhysicsActorWeldRoot(), [&](const FPhysicsActorHandle& Actor)
	{
		ApplyMaterialToInstanceShapes_AssumesLocked(SimplePhysMat, ComplexPhysMats, ComplexPhysMatMasks);
	});
}

void FBodyInstance::InvalidateCollisionProfileName()
{
	CollisionProfileName = UCollisionProfile::CustomCollisionProfileName;
	ExternalCollisionProfileBodySetup = nullptr;
	bPendingCollisionProfileSetup = false;
}
```

```
	Chaos_Emission_Pattern_On_Demand UMETA(DisplayName = "On Demand"),
	//
	Chaos_Max                UMETA(Hidden)
};


UENUM(BlueprintType)
enum class EDamageModelTypeEnum : uint8
{
	/** Using damage threshold set based on level of the cluster */
	Chaos_Damage_Model_UserDefined_Damage_Threshold UMETA(DisplayName = "User-Defined Damage Threshold"),

	/** Using damage threshold set using the physical material strength and how connected a cluster is */
	Chaos_Damage_Model_Material_Strength_And_Connectivity_DamageThreshold UMETA(DisplayName = "Material Strength And Connectivity Damage Threshold"),

	Chaos_Max UMETA(Hidden)
};

// convert user level damage model to chaos damage evaluation model
inline Chaos::EDamageEvaluationModel GetDamageEvaluationModel(const EDamageModelTypeEnum DamageModel)
{
	switch (DamageModel)
	{
	case EDamageModelTypeEnum::Chaos_Damage_Model_UserDefined_Damage_Threshold: 
		return Chaos::EDamageEvaluationModel::StrainFromDamageThreshold;
	case EDamageModelTypeEnum::Chaos_Damage_Model_Material_Strength_And_Connectivity_DamageThreshold: 
		return Chaos::EDamageEvaluationModel::StrainFromMaterialStrengthAndConnectivity;
	default:
		ensure(false); // unexpected
		return Chaos::EDamageEvaluationModel::StrainFromDamageThreshold;
	}
}
```

```
---
name: unreal-editor-control
description: Use whenever operating, inspecting, modifying, or automating content through Unreal Engine's UE5 Editor, including actors, assets, levels, Blueprints, materials, Sequencer, Niagara, PCG, UMG, and other editor operations, and when choosing which Unreal control surface or MCP server to use. Do not use for engine source edits, builds, packaging, runtime-only debugging, or crash analysis.
---

# Unreal Editor control

Choose the narrowest surface that can complete the task.

This routes operations through Unreal Editor. Repository changes, engine builds,
runtime debugging, and crash analysis need their own development tools.

For creating or scaffolding a new project, invoke the `ue-project-create` skill.
Project creation is a template transformation and does not require a running
editor.

## Configure gotcha reporting once per session

If the `ue-editor-control:ue-gotcha-reporter` custom agent is available and the
conversation does not already contain a gotcha-reporting preference, ask the
user once, before substantial editor work, to choose:

- **File qualified gotchas automatically** after a capability preflight and
  deduplication.
- **Do not track gotchas** in this session.

Keep the choice in conversation context for this session only. Do not persist
it or ask again. If interactive consent cannot be obtained, default to **Do not
track gotchas**; never infer permission to create issues.

For automatic filing, immediately delegate a request containing
`operation: preflight` and `consent: file` to
`ue-editor-control:ue-gotcha-reporter` in the background and continue the main
task. Do not file until it reports that repository lookup works and the native
issue-creation tool is available. A side-effect-free preflight cannot prove
write authorization; if the first creation attempt fails, disable gotcha
tracking for the rest of the session.

If preflight cannot establish capability, silently disable gotcha tracking for
the session. Do not interrupt the main task or notify the user unless they ask
about reporting status. Disabled mode does not need preflight.

During later work, treat a discovery as a gotcha candidate only when it
invalidated a reasonable assumption, the missing or misleading information
caused significant lost time or repeated attempts, and preserving it could
improve this plugin's tools, diagnostics, or skills. Do not report ordinary
bugs, user mistakes, already-documented behavior, speculation, or unrelated
Unreal facts.

When reporting is enabled, delegate qualified candidates to the reporter in the
background and continue the main task. Include `operation: report`, the selected
`consent: file` mode, ready preflight status, the prior assumption, observed
behavior and evidence, time or iterations lost, Unreal/plugin versions and
environment, and the expected plugin relevance.

## 1. Prefer `ue-editor-control`

If the `ue-editor-control` MCP server exposes `editor_status`,
`editor_select`, and `editor_launch`, use it instead of a directly registered
raw Unreal endpoint. Start with `editor_status`.

The proxy keeps the UE tool catalog available while no editor is running,
discovers and attributes editors, reconnects after restarts, selects among
projects, and launches editors safely. If status says `LIVE (degraded)`, continue
through the proxy but follow the reported catalog-mismatch remediation.

## 2. Raw UE 5.8 MCP is a registered fallback only

A direct raw UE registration exposes `list_toolsets`, `describe_toolset`, and
`call_tool` in another MCP server namespace, without the proxy's `editor_*`
tools. Use it directly only when it is already registered and the proxy is not
available. A raw endpoint cannot be conjured by calling its meta-tools; if
neither surface exists, use the `ue-editor-launch` skill when available or
explain that an Unreal MCP connection must be configured.

If both registrations exist, duplicate meta-tool names appear in two server
namespaces while only `ue-editor-control` has `editor_status`. Use the proxy and
suggest that the user remove or disable the **direct client registration** for
the raw endpoint. Do not stop or disable UE's in-editor MCP server: it is the
proxy's upstream dependency. Never change client configuration without the
user's direction.

## 3. Discover typed tools before acting

Call `list_toolsets`, then `describe_toolset` only for the relevant domain.
Invoke tools through `call_tool`. Do not eagerly load every toolset schema.

## 4. Batch through `ProgrammaticToolset`

Use `editor_toolset.toolsets.programmatic.ProgrammaticToolset` when loops,
branching, local data flow, or several typed calls would otherwise require many
round trips.

Call `get_execution_environment` once before `execute_tool_script`. Follow its
current instructions, and inspect output schemas for any called tools whose
results the script will parse. This remains sandboxed orchestration of registered
tools, not unrestricted editor Python.

## 5. Escalate only when typed tools cannot do the work

Python Remote Execution is the unrestricted escape hatch and requires explicit
user intent. Invoke the `python-remote-execution` skill before enabling or using
it. Do not substitute it merely because a typed tool requires schema discovery.

For editor startup, selection, or connectivity failures, invoke the
`ue-editor-launch` skill rather than duplicating its diagnostics here.
```

```
# GitHub Copilot CLI Documentation

## README

## Help Command Output
Global
  /help - show full help
  ? - show quick help
  / - commands
  @ - mention files
  # - mention issues and pull requests
  ! - execute shell command
  shift+tab - switch modes
  ctrl+s - stash/pop current prompt
  ctrl+q - enqueue prompt
  ctrl+r - reverse search history
  ctrl+o - toggle all timeline
  ctrl+c - cancel
  ctrl+c×2 - exit
  esc esc - clear input, interrupt, stop agents, or rewind
  ctrl+d - shutdown
  ctrl+z - suspend
  ctrl+l - clear screen
  ctrl+t - toggle reasoning display
  ctrl+x → b - move current task to background
  ctrl+x → g - collapse or expand the autopilot goal panel
  ctrl+x → o - open most recent link

Input
  ctrl+a - go to line start
  ctrl+e - go to line end
  ctrl+h - delete previous character
  ctrl+w - delete previous word
  ctrl+u - delete from cursor to beginning of line
  ctrl+k - delete from cursor to end of line
  meta+←/→ - move cursor by word
  shift+enter - insert newline
  ctrl+g - edit prompt in $EDITOR

Agent Environment
  /init - Initialize Copilot instructions for this repository
  /agent - Browse and select agents: /agent [name]
  /skills - Manage skills for enhanced capabilities
  /mcp - Manage MCP server configuration
  /plugin - Manage plugins and plugin marketplaces

Agents / Subagents
  /model - Select the AI model for this session (use 'auto' to let Copilot pick automatically). Use /config model to set the user default, '--repo'/'--local' to set the repo default, or 'plan'/'--plan' to set the plan-mode model.
  /delegate - Send this session to GitHub and Copilot will create a PR; use --base to choose the PR target branch
  /fleet - Enable fleet mode for parallel subagent execution
  /autopilot - Toggle autopilot mode, or set an autopilot objective with an optional AI-credit limit (--max-ai-credits)
  /tasks - View and manage tasks (subagents and shell commands)

Code
  /ide - Connect to an IDE workspace
  /diff - Review the changes made in the current directory
  /pr - Operate on pull requests for the current branch
  /review - Run code review agent to analyze changes
  /security-review - Analyze staged and unstaged changes for security vulnerabilities.
  /rubber-duck - Get an independent critique of your current work from the rubber duck agent
  /lsp - Manage language server configuration
  /terminal-setup - Configure terminal for multiline input support (shift+enter)

Permissions
  /permissions - Switch between permission modes
  /allow-all - Enable all permissions (tools, paths, and URLs)
  /add-dir - Allow file access to a directory and load its .github skills and agents as trusted configuration
  /list-dirs - Display all allowed directories for file access
  /cwd - Change working directory or show current directory
  /reset-allowed-tools - Reset the list of allowed tools

Session
  /resume - Switch to a different session (optionally specify session ID, task ID, or name)
  /rename - Rename the current session, or auto-generate a name from conversation
  /fork - Fork the current session into a new session, optionally with a name
  /context - Show context window token usage and visualization
  /usage - Display session usage metrics and statistics
  /session - View and manage sessions. Use subcommands for details.
  /compact - Summarize conversation history to reduce context window usage. Optionally provide focus instructions.
  /share - Share session or research report to a markdown file, HTML file, GitHub gist, or a shareable GitHub link
  /remote - Share this session: remote control from GitHub web and mobile, or directly with another CLI
  /copy - Copy the last response to the clipboard
  /rewind - Rewind the last turn and revert file changes

Help
  /help - Show help for interactive commands
  /changelog - Display changelog for CLI versions. Add 'summarize' to get an AI summary.
  /feedback - Provide feedback about the CLI
  /diagnose - Analyze the current session log, optionally with a custom prompt
  /theme - View or set color mode
  /statusline - Configure status line items
  /footer - Configure status line items
  /update - Update the CLI to the latest version
  /version - Display version information and check for updates
  /experimental - Show available experimental features, or enable/disable experimental mode
  /memory - Show memory status, or enable/disable memory across sessions
  /clear - Abandon this session and start fresh
  /instructions - View and toggle custom instruction files
  /app - Prefer a visual workspace? Try out the GitHub Copilot desktop app

Other commands
  /ask - Ask a quick side question without adding to conversation history
  /chronicle - Session history tools and insights
  /env - Show loaded environment details (instructions, MCP servers, skills, agents, hooks, plugins, LSPs, extensions)
  /exit - Exit the CLI; use 'print' to print the session after exiting alt screen
  /keep-alive - Manage keep-alive mode (prevents system sleep).
  /limits - View or edit session limits; the AI Credit limit is a soft cap
  /login - Log in to Copilot
  /logout - Log out of an OAuth login session
  /new - Start a new conversation
  /plan - Create an implementation plan before coding
  /refine - Rewrite a rough, stream-of-consciousness prompt into a clear one for review (Ctrl+X / then /refine cleans up your current input)
  /research - Run deep research investigation using GitHub search and web sources
  /restart - Restart the CLI, restoring supported live sessions in this process
  /search - Search the conversation timeline
  /settings - Open the settings UI, show, set, or unset a single value ('/settings unset <key>' removes it). Use '--repo'/'--local' to target repo settings.
  /subagents - Configure default and per-agent subagent models
  /user - Manage GitHub user list
  /vim - Toggle Vim mode for the input (hjkl/w/b/e/ge/0/^/$/gg/G motions, f/F/t/T/;/, char search, i/a/o insert, r/~/J/x/D/C edit, d/c/y operators, y/p/P yank & put, . repeat, u/ctrl+r undo & redo, counts, esc for normal mode)
  /voice - Manage voice mode (dictation transcription via Foundry Local)

  .github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md (in git root & cwd)

  $HOME/.copilot/instructions/**/*.instructions.md
```

```
# Dublin Flight - checkpoint 00

Date: September 8, 2026
Status: template creation and pristine C++ build passed; editor startup in progress.
No playable game or performance claim yet.

## Success and validation loop

The objective is an immersive UE 5.8 flight game over accurately textured Dublin:
bounded-speed aircraft controls, a simple HUD, stationary/repositionable god mode,
localised cannon damage, gravity bombs with configurable game-only TNT yield,
collapsing buildings, actual terrain craters, and water plumes and spreading waves.
Destruction must look stunning without sacrificing the requested 60 FPS floor.

Each playable slice must have acceptance criteria established before implementation,
automated coverage for code changes, an in-editor gameplay exercise, an explicit
asset/project save, and reviewed screenshot evidence. Performance remains
unverified until representative flight and destruction workloads are measured
on this machine at recorded resolution and rendering settings.

## Verified prerequisites and selected creation plan

- Engine: C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8.
- Installed template: Games / TP_Blank, C++, base variant.
- Project name: DublinFlight.
- Destination: C:\Code\tmp\messing\dublin-lidar\DublinFlight (must not already exist).
- Desktop hardware target, maximum initial quality; actual game settings will
  be selected from measured results.
- MCP configuration will be written: port 8000, auto-start and tool search enabled.
- Toolset tier: all.
- PythonScriptPlugin and EditorScriptingUtilities enabled for supported editor
  tool dependencies only. Unrestricted Python Remote Execution stays disabled.
- Explicit plugin additions: EnhancedInput, GeometryCollectionPlugin,
  FieldSystemPlugin, Niagara, ProceduralMeshComponent.
- The complete template inspection resolved the selected plugins with no warnings.
- Installed TP_TopDownBP was excluded by the creation script because its
  TemplateDefs.ini is malformed. It is not used by this project.
- C++ project generation and compilation are separate steps after creation.
- No gotcha reports or other GitHub issues will be filed.

Observed machine: Intel i9-13950HX, approximately 64 GB RAM, NVIDIA RTX 4090
Laptop GPU (also an integrated Intel GPU). This is hardware discovery, not evidence
that the requested frame rate has been met.

## Work underway

Two Astra agents, each configured with long context and xhigh reasoning, are
independently recovering the prior Dublin imagery/LiDAR pipeline and investigating
the native destruction/effects implementation and performance constraints.

First playable slice acceptance: a saved UE 5.8 map with a controllable aircraft,
limited speed suitable for the city footprint, readable HUD, and a toggle that
holds the player stationary in the sky while still permitting aiming and weapons.
This slice must be exercised in PIE before proceeding to city/destruction work.

## Build and launch evidence

The pristine DublinFlightEditor Win64 Development target built successfully with
UE 5.8. Project generation took 25.05 seconds; compilation/linking took
73.03 seconds. Both returned exit code 0. The project DLL and module manifest were
verified. No project/source/config files changed during this baseline build.

Non-blocking warnings: Visual Studio 2022 cannot include .NET 10 C# projects, so
automation solutions target Visual Studio 2026; StructUtils deprecation warnings.

The editor was launched through ue-editor-control on port 8000, explicitly passing
python_remote_execution=false. MCP connectivity and the available typed toolsets
are not yet verified.

NVIDIA's own utility confirms 16,376 MiB dedicated GPU memory. The earlier generic
Windows GPU-memory field was not used to infer VRAM.

The city-data investigation now explicitly includes OpenStreetMap footprint
constraints, fused with LiDAR heights and roof detail, to reduce noisy triangular
building silhouettes. Imagery/footprint coverage and licensing remain under review.

No screenshots are available yet: editor startup must finish first.
```

````
# ue-editor-control

Control the Unreal Engine editor from an AI agent.

This plugin bridges to the editor's built-in MCP server and keeps its tools
available whether or not an editor is running. Clients connect to MCP servers
once, at startup, so a server whose upstream is absent at that moment is normally
dead for the whole session. This one answers `initialize` and `tools/list` from a
catalog embedded in its own binary, then connects to an editor as soon as one
appears — with no agent restart.

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `list_toolsets` | List the editor's toolsets |
| `describe_toolset` | Get a toolset's tools and input schemas |
| `call_tool` | Invoke a tool from a toolset |
| `editor_status` | Report running editors, the bound one, and any problems |
| `editor_select` | Bind a specific editor by project slug |
| `editor_launch` | Launch an editor for a project, with MCP enabled; optionally force Python Remote Execution on or off for that process |

The first three are the editor's own tools, passed through unchanged. The
toolsets behind them are discovered per call rather than mirrored, so toolsets
and tools that differ between engine versions are picked up as they are, with no
update to this plugin and no restart.

These six are fixed for the lifetime of the plugin. If an editor's definitions
differ, calls are still delivered and `editor_status` reports the connection as
`LIVE (degraded)`, naming each difference; the fix is a plugin update.

## Agent guidance

- `unreal-editor-control` — the broad starting point for Unreal Editor work;
  selects between the proxy, direct raw MCP, sandboxed tool orchestration, and
  Python Remote Execution.
- `ue-editor-launch` — starting an editor with MCP enabled, and diagnosing one
  that is running but not serving.
- `ue-project-create` — creating UE 5.8 projects from installed engine templates
  without starting the editor.
- `python-remote-execution` — inspecting, configuring, and using Unreal's
  unrestricted Python Remote Execution channel.

In GitHub Copilot clients, `unreal-editor-control` asks once per session whether
to file qualified gotchas automatically or disable tracking. Automatic filing
starts with a capability preflight. The **UE Gotcha Reporter** checks open and
closed issues, removes private project details, and creates a `gotcha` issue
when the finding is novel and actionable. Missing access or a failed creation
silently disables reporting for the session.

## Getting started

Enable MCP in your Unreal project: *Project Settings → Plugins → Model Context
Protocol* → turn on **Auto Start Server** and **Enable Tool Search**, then restart
the editor. Call `editor_status` at any time to see what is detected and what, if
anything, needs fixing.

If you run several editors at once, give each project a distinct **Server Port
Number**. Unreal binds its routes without checking that the listener started, so
two editors sharing a port leaves the second one silently unreachable.

`editor_launch` will not start an editor whose engine cannot serve MCP — an
engine that ships the plugin but has not built it, or built it against a
different engine version, produces an editor that stops on a *Missing Modules*
dialog instead of listening.

`editor_launch` accepts an optional `python_remote_execution` boolean. `true`
forces the channel on, `false` forces it off, and omission inherits the saved
configuration. The channel is unauthenticated and executes unrestricted Python
with the full `unreal` API for the editor's lifetime.

The `python-remote-execution` skill includes `Get-PythonRemoteExecution.ps1`,
which reports the layered setting and its provenance, and
`Set-PythonRemoteExecution.ps1`, which changes an explicitly selected ini layer.

The `ue-project-create` skill lists and inspects templates from a selected UE 5.8
engine, then creates a Blueprint or C++ project at an explicit new destination.
It configures MCP tool-search access on port 8000 by default; `--mcp-port`
selects another port and `--no-mcp` leaves template-provided MCP settings
unchanged. It also enables the MCP plugin, toolset tier `all`, and the Python
editor scripting plugins. `--toolsets none|most|all`, `--no-python`, and
repeatable `--add-plugin NAME` options customize the plugin plan. Python plugin
enablement does not enable Python Remote Execution. C++ project-file generation
and compilation remain separate.

## Configuration

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `UE_EDITOR_MCP_URL` | Connect to this endpoint only; disables discovery |
| `UE_EDITOR_PROJECT` | Bind this project slug or `.uproject` path |
| `UE_EDITOR_LOG` | `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace` |

## Diagnostics

```
bin\win32-x64\ue-editor-control.exe doctor
```

Reports the advertised tools, every editor found, its configured and actual
ports, its settings, and the result of probing each endpoint.

---

Microsoft Internal Only. See `LICENSE`.

Source, tests and build instructions: see the repository this plugin ships from.
````

```
# Dublin Flight - checkpoint 00

Date: September 8, 2026
Status: template creation and pristine C++ build passed; editor startup finished.
Blocked: required editor tools cannot be discovered in the resumed Copilot CLI
session, despite the plugin being installed, connected and bound to the editor.
No playable game or performance claim yet.

## Success and validation loop

The objective is an immersive UE 5.8 flight game over accurately textured Dublin:
bounded-speed aircraft controls, a simple HUD, stationary/repositionable god mode,
localised cannon damage, gravity bombs with configurable game-only TNT yield,
collapsing buildings, actual terrain craters, and water plumes and spreading waves.
Destruction must look stunning without sacrificing the requested 60 FPS floor.

Each playable slice must have acceptance criteria established before implementation,
automated coverage for code changes, an in-editor gameplay exercise, an explicit
asset/project save, and reviewed screenshot evidence. Performance remains
unverified until representative flight and destruction workloads are measured
on this machine at recorded resolution and rendering settings.

## Verified prerequisites and selected creation plan

- Engine: C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8.
- Installed template: Games / TP_Blank, C++, base variant.
- Project name: DublinFlight.
- Destination: C:\Code\tmp\messing\dublin-lidar\DublinFlight (must not already exist).
- Desktop hardware target, maximum initial quality; actual game settings will
  be selected from measured results.
- MCP configuration will be written: port 8000, auto-start and tool search enabled.
- Toolset tier: all.
- PythonScriptPlugin and EditorScriptingUtilities enabled for supported editor
  tool dependencies only. Unrestricted Python Remote Execution stays disabled.
- Explicit plugin additions: EnhancedInput, GeometryCollectionPlugin,
  FieldSystemPlugin, Niagara, ProceduralMeshComponent.
- The complete template inspection resolved the selected plugins with no warnings.
- Installed TP_TopDownBP was excluded by the creation script because its
  TemplateDefs.ini is malformed. It is not used by this project.
- C++ project generation and compilation are separate steps after creation.
- No gotcha reports or other GitHub issues will be filed.

Observed machine: Intel i9-13950HX, approximately 64 GB RAM, NVIDIA RTX 4090
Laptop GPU (also an integrated Intel GPU). This is hardware discovery, not evidence
that the requested frame rate has been met.

## Research recovery status

Two Astra agents, each configured with long context and xhigh reasoning, were
independently recovering the prior Dublin imagery/LiDAR pipeline and investigating
the native destruction/effects implementation and performance constraints.
After the CLI crash, their handles and the build agent handle return "No agent
found", including when retried after the user approved YOLO permissions. The
pristine build and startup observation logs persist; final research reports have
not been recovered. Do not assume those investigations finished successfully.

First playable slice acceptance: a saved UE 5.8 map with a controllable aircraft,
limited speed suitable for the city footprint, readable HUD, and a toggle that
holds the player stationary in the sky while still permitting aiming and weapons.
This slice must be exercised in PIE before proceeding to city/destruction work.

## Build and launch evidence

The pristine DublinFlightEditor Win64 Development target built successfully with
UE 5.8. Project generation took 25.05 seconds; compilation/linking took
73.03 seconds. Both returned exit code 0. The project DLL and module manifest were
verified. No project/source/config files changed during this baseline build.

Non-blocking warnings: Visual Studio 2022 cannot include .NET 10 C# projects, so
automation solutions target Visual Studio 2026; StructUtils deprecation warnings.

The editor was launched through ue-editor-control on port 8000, explicitly passing
python_remote_execution=false. On recovery, the plugin's bundled doctor verified
that the editor is serving MCP on port 8000, and its three upstream meta-tools
match the plugin's advertised catalog. Individual editor toolsets and gameplay
operations are not yet verified.
```

```
# Dublin Flight - first playable slice acceptance

Status: specified, not implemented or verified.
Date: September 8, 2026

This is an incremental control/HUD milestone, not the completed game. It does not
satisfy the city, weapons, destruction, visual-quality or 60 FPS acceptance gates.

## Required experience

- Start PIE in a saved project map and possess the aircraft automatically.
- Fly using pitch, roll, yaw and throttle controls, with a readable chase camera.
- Use centimetres internally and metres/metres per second in the HUD.
- Start at 40 m/s, with a deliberately restrained 20-65 m/s flight speed range.
  Revisit those limits against the recovered city extent before the city milestone.
- Toggle god mode with G: preserve the current position/orientation, stop flight
  translation, allow aiming and deliberate repositioning, and remain stationary
  when no movement input is given. Resume flight without teleporting.
- Reset safely to the original spawn using Home.
- Display mode, speed, altitude, compass heading and a centre aiming reticle.
- Keep controls visible in a compact help panel. Do not claim that weapons work
  before their implementation milestone.
- Use a recognisable aircraft silhouette for this slice; the final aircraft,
  materials and effects must pass a later visual review.

## Native and gameplay checks

Automated coverage must exercise throttle bounds, flight integration, finite
transforms, bounded frame-step integration, reset and mode transitions. Verify
that stationary god mode drifts less than 1 cm over five seconds without input,
and that deliberate repositioning and aiming still work.

Exercise actual input in PIE: take control, change pitch/bank/yaw/throttle, toggle
god mode, hold still, reposition, aim, resume flight and reset. A compiled test
or successful actor spawn is not a substitute for this gameplay exercise.

Explicitly save the level and modified assets, capture a gameplay screenshot, and
review the camera/HUD/readability before advancing. Record any unverified checks
instead of treating them as passed.

## Scope and implementation boundaries

Use native C++ for runtime simulation and automated tests, and ue-editor-control
typed tools for editor assets, level assembly, gameplay exercise and screenshots.
Do not enable unrestricted Python Remote Execution.

Avoid concurrent mutation of editor state: the coordinator owns editor calls.
Implementation agents will have disjoint source-file ownership and use the
same native interface contract before implementation begins. Builds will be
serialized after their changes are integrated.

Current prerequisite: the pristine project compiled successfully. The launched
editor is still starting/compiling initial shaders; a live MCP catalog has not
yet been confirmed. Implementation handoff remains gated on that check.
```

```
# Dublin Flight - first playable slice acceptance

Status: specified, not implemented or verified.
Date: September 8, 2026

This is an incremental control/HUD milestone, not the completed game. It does not
satisfy the city, weapons, destruction, visual-quality or 60 FPS acceptance gates.

## Required experience

- Start PIE in a saved project map and possess the aircraft automatically.
- Fly using pitch, roll, yaw and throttle controls, with a readable chase camera.
- Use centimetres internally and metres/metres per second in the HUD.
- Start at 40 m/s, with a deliberately restrained 20-65 m/s flight speed range.
  Revisit those limits against the recovered city extent before the city milestone.
- Toggle god mode with G: preserve the current position/orientation, stop flight
  translation, allow aiming and deliberate repositioning, and remain stationary
  when no movement input is given. Resume flight without teleporting.
- Reset safely to the original spawn using Home.
- Display mode, speed, altitude, compass heading and a centre aiming reticle.
- Keep controls visible in a compact help panel. Do not claim that weapons work
  before their implementation milestone.
- Use a recognisable aircraft silhouette for this slice; the final aircraft,
  materials and effects must pass a later visual review.

## Native and gameplay checks

Automated coverage must exercise throttle bounds, flight integration, finite
transforms, bounded frame-step integration, reset and mode transitions. Verify
that stationary god mode drifts less than 1 cm over five seconds without input,
and that deliberate repositioning and aiming still work.

Exercise actual input in PIE: take control, change pitch/bank/yaw/throttle, toggle
god mode, hold still, reposition, aim, resume flight and reset. A compiled test
or successful actor spawn is not a substitute for this gameplay exercise.

Explicitly save the level and modified assets, capture a gameplay screenshot, and
review the camera/HUD/readability before advancing. Record any unverified checks
instead of treating them as passed.

## Scope and implementation boundaries

Use native C++ for runtime simulation and automated tests, and ue-editor-control
typed tools for editor assets, level assembly, gameplay exercise and screenshots.
Do not enable unrestricted Python Remote Execution.

Avoid concurrent mutation of editor state: the coordinator owns editor calls.
Implementation agents will have disjoint source-file ownership and use the
same native interface contract before implementation begins. Builds will be
serialized after their changes are integrated.

Current prerequisite: the pristine project compiled successfully. On September 8,
at approximately 17:27 local time, editor_status reported LIVE and list_toolsets
successfully returned the supported catalog for the existing DublinFlight editor.
The prior tool-discovery blocker is cleared.

## Implementation handoff and readiness review

One implementation agent owns the complete first-slice native runtime and tests,
avoiding split ownership of flight/HUD interfaces. It must not mutate editor
assets, launch editors, build concurrently, or modify engine files. The
coordinator owns level creation, integration builds and editor validation.

Controls: W/S pitch, A/D roll, Q/E yaw; Shift/Ctrl increase/decrease throttle;
G toggles god mode; Home resets. In god mode W/S moves forward/back, A/D strafes,
Space/C moves up/down, and mouse axes aim. Alternate arrow-key pitch/roll is
acceptable. Display mode-specific controls so the dual meanings are clear.

The native pawn must expose readable mode, speed and flight state, with callable
toggle/reset methods for automated tests. Keep input, flight integration and
presentation separated. Use a deterministic testable flight-state helper with
finite-input guards and bounded substeps; do not discard normal frame time.
God-mode no-input translation must be exactly zero. Sweep movement against world
collision, preventing penetration and resetting safely on a flight collision.

The pawn automatically builds a simple aircraft silhouette from existing engine
primitive meshes for this first slice. The native game mode supplies pawn/HUD
classes; the coordinator assembles a saved map using typed editor tools.

Readiness verdict: Ready for this bounded slice. Runtime API/state and file
ownership are contained within one agent. Native and PIE acceptance are specified.
Azure, network API and identity review are not applicable. The final city extent,
real aircraft art, weapons, terrain and water effects remain later-slice work,
not hidden assumptions in this implementation handoff.
```

```
/** Utility delegate class to allow binding to either a C++ function or a blueprint script delegate */
template<class DelegateType, class DynamicDelegateType>
struct TInputUnifiedDelegate
{
	TInputUnifiedDelegate() {};
	TInputUnifiedDelegate(DelegateType D) : FuncDelegate(MakeShared<DelegateType>(MoveTemp(D))) {};
	TInputUnifiedDelegate(DynamicDelegateType D) : FuncDynDelegate(MakeShared<DynamicDelegateType>(MoveTemp(D))) {};

	/** Returns if either the native or dynamic delegate is bound */
	inline bool IsBound() const
	{
		return ((FuncDelegate.IsValid() && FuncDelegate->IsBound()) || (FuncDynDelegate.IsValid() && FuncDynDelegate->IsBound()));
	}

	/** Returns the UObject that this delegate is bound to. */
	inline UObject* GetUObject() const
	{
		if (FuncDelegate.IsValid())
		{
			if (FuncDelegate->IsBound())
			{
				return FuncDelegate->GetUObject();
			}
		}
		else if (FuncDynDelegate.IsValid())
		{
			if (FuncDynDelegate->IsBound())
			{
				return FuncDynDelegate->GetUObject();
			}
		}
		
		return nullptr;
	}
	
	/** Returns if either the native or dynamic delegate is bound to an object */
	inline bool IsBoundToObject(void const* Object) const
	{
		if (FuncDelegate.IsValid())
		{
			if (FuncDelegate->IsBound())
			{
				return FuncDelegate->IsBoundToObject(Object);
			}
		}
		else if (FuncDynDelegate.IsValid())
		{
			if (FuncDynDelegate->IsBound())
			{
				return FuncDynDelegate->IsBoundToObject(Object);
			}
		}

		return false;
	}

	/** Binds a native delegate and unbinds any bound dynamic delegate */
	template< class UserClass >
	inline void BindDelegate(UserClass* Object, typename DelegateType::template TMethodPtr< UserClass > Func)
	{
		FuncDynDelegate.Reset();;
		FuncDelegate = MakeShared<DelegateType>(DelegateType::CreateUObject(Object, Func));
	}

	/** Binds a dynamic delegate and unbinds any bound native delegate */
	inline void BindDelegate(UObject* Object, const FName FuncName)
	{
		FuncDelegate.Reset();
		FuncDynDelegate = MakeShared<DynamicDelegateType>();
		FuncDynDelegate->BindUFunction(Object, FuncName);
	}

	/** Returns a reference to the native delegate and unbinds any bound dynamic delegate */
	DelegateType& GetDelegateForManualSet()
	{
		FuncDynDelegate.Reset();
		FuncDelegate = MakeShared<DelegateType>();
		return *FuncDelegate;
	}

	/** Unbinds any bound delegates */
	inline void Unbind()
	{
		FuncDelegate.Reset();
		FuncDynDelegate.Reset();
	}

	/** Returns a const reference to the Function Delegate. */
	inline const DelegateType& GetDelegate() const
	{
		return (FuncDelegate.IsValid() ? *FuncDelegate : UnboundDelegate);
	}

	/** Returns a const reference to the Dynamic Function Delegate. */
	inline const DynamicDelegateType& GetDynamicDelegate() const
	{
		return (FuncDynDelegate.IsValid() ? *FuncDynDelegate : UnboundDynamicDelegate);
	}

protected:
	/** Holds the delegate to call. */
	TSharedPtr<DelegateType> FuncDelegate;
	/** Holds the dynamic delegate to call. */
	TSharedPtr<DynamicDelegateType> FuncDynDelegate;

	static const DelegateType UnboundDelegate;
	static const DynamicDelegateType UnboundDynamicDelegate;
};
```

```
	FPawnRestartedSignature ReceiveRestartedDelegate;

	/**
	 * Notifies other systems that a pawn has been restarted. By default this is called on the server for all pawns and the owning client for player pawns.
```

### Copilot

The runtime source is persisted. Held controls must be released after a mode change or reset so a flight input cannot become unintended god-mode movement; an obstructed spawn leaves the pawn stationary in god mode rather than teleporting into collision. I’m adding deterministic coverage and an isolated transient-world integration test, without running either.

```
// Copyright Epic Games, Inc. All Rights Reserved.

#pragma once

#include "Templates/SubclassOf.h"

/** Struct containing a collection of optional parameters for initialization of a World. */
struct FWorldInitializationValues
{
	FWorldInitializationValues()
		: bInitializeScenes(true)
		, bAllowAudioPlayback(true)
		, bRequiresHitProxies(true)
		, bCreatePhysicsScene(true)
		, bCreateNavigation(true)
		, bCreateAISystem(true)
		, bShouldSimulatePhysics(true)
		, bEnableTraceCollision(false)
		, bForceUseMovementComponentInNonGameWorld(false)
		, bTransactional(true)
		, bCreateFXSystem(true)
		, bCreateWorldPartition(false)
		, bEnableWorldPartitionStreaming(true)
		, bAllowLumenPrimitiveTrackingInPreviewWorld(false)
	{
	}

	/** Should the scenes (physics, rendering) be created. */
	uint32 bInitializeScenes:1;

	/** Are sounds allowed to be generated from this world. */
	uint32 bAllowAudioPlayback:1;

	/** Should the render scene create hit proxies. */
	uint32 bRequiresHitProxies:1;

	/** Should the physics scene be created. bInitializeScenes must be true for this to be considered. */
	uint32 bCreatePhysicsScene:1;

	/** Should the navigation system be created for this world. */
	uint32 bCreateNavigation:1;

	/** Should the AI system be created for this world. */
	uint32 bCreateAISystem:1;

	/** Should physics be simulated in this world. */
	uint32 bShouldSimulatePhysics:1;

	/** Are collision trace calls valid within this world. */
	uint32 bEnableTraceCollision:1;

	/** Special flag to enable movement component in non game worlds (see UMovementComponent::OnRegister) */
	uint32 bForceUseMovementComponentInNonGameWorld:1;

	/** Should actions performed to objects in this world be saved to the transaction buffer. */
	uint32 bTransactional:1;

	/** Should the FX system be created for this world. */
	uint32 bCreateFXSystem:1;

	/** Should the world be partitioned */
	uint32 bCreateWorldPartition:1;

	/** If bCreateWorldPartition is set to true, this flag will init the streaming mode for the WorldPartition object (default to true to preserve previous behavior) */
	uint32 bEnableWorldPartitionStreaming:1;

	/** Allows LumenSceneData to set bTrackAllPrimitives even if the world is a preview world. This makes it possible to populate the Lumen surface cache and use Lumen in preview worlds, e.g. asset editor viewports. */
	uint32 bAllowLumenPrimitiveTrackingInPreviewWorld : 1;

	/** The default game mode for this world (if any) */
	TSubclassOf<class AGameModeBase> DefaultGameMode;

	FWorldInitializationValues& InitializeScenes(const bool bInitialize) { bInitializeScenes = bInitialize; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& AllowAudioPlayback(const bool bAllow) { bAllowAudioPlayback = bAllow; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& RequiresHitProxies(const bool bRequires) { bRequiresHitProxies = bRequires; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& CreatePhysicsScene(const bool bCreate) { bCreatePhysicsScene = bCreate; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& CreateNavigation(const bool bCreate) { bCreateNavigation = bCreate; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& CreateAISystem(const bool bCreate) { bCreateAISystem = bCreate; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& ShouldSimulatePhysics(const bool bInShouldSimulatePhysics) { bShouldSimulatePhysics = bInShouldSimulatePhysics; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& EnableTraceCollision(const bool bInEnableTraceCollision) { bEnableTraceCollision = bInEnableTraceCollision; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& ForceUseMovementComponentInNonGameWorld(const bool bInForceUseMovementComponentInNonGameWorld) { bForceUseMovementComponentInNonGameWorld = bInForceUseMovementComponentInNonGameWorld; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& SetTransactional(const bool bInTransactional) { bTransactional = bInTransactional; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& CreateFXSystem(const bool bCreate) { bCreateFXSystem = bCreate; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& CreateWorldPartition(const bool bCreate) { bCreateWorldPartition = bCreate; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& EnableWorldPartitionStreaming(const bool bEnableStreaming) { bEnableWorldPartitionStreaming = bEnableStreaming; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& AllowLumenPrimitiveTrackingInPreviewWorld(const bool bAllowLumenPrimitiveTracking) { bAllowLumenPrimitiveTrackingInPreviewWorld = bAllowLumenPrimitiveTracking; return *this; }
	FWorldInitializationValues& SetDefaultGameMode(TSubclassOf<class AGameModeBase> GameMode) { DefaultGameMode = GameMode; return *this; }
};
```

```
"""Prepare georeferenced imagery and LiDAR for the Dublin glass study."""
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import requests
from PIL import Image
from pyproj import Transformer
from scipy.ndimage import map_coordinates

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ASSETS = ROOT / "assets"
ASSETS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
CENTER = (315989.0, 234393.0)
RADIUS = 760
BOUNDS = (CENTER[0] - 800, CENTER[1] - 800,
          CENTER[0] + 800, CENTER[1] + 800)
SESSION = requests.Session()
SESSION.headers["User-Agent"] = "DublinLidarGlobe/1.0 (local artistic visualization)"


def fetch_sources():
    base = "https://services.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer"
    response = SESSION.get(base, params={"f": "json"}, timeout=90)
    response.raise_for_status()
    service = response.json()
    (ASSETS / "imagery-service.json").write_text(json.dumps(service, indent=2))
    print("Imagery:", service.get("copyrightText"), flush=True)
    # Request native Web Mercator imagery, then rectify to the LiDAR grid locally.
    mercator = Transformer.from_crs(29903, 3857, always_xy=True)
    corners = np.array([mercator.transform(x, y) for x in BOUNDS[::2] for y in BOUNDS[1::2]])
    box = (*corners.min(axis=0), *corners.max(axis=0))
    response = SESSION.get(base + "/export", params={
        "bbox": ",".join(map(str, box)), "bboxSR": 3857, "imageSR": 3857,
        "size": "2048,2048", "format": "jpg", "f": "json",
    }, timeout=120)
    response.raise_for_status()
    metadata = response.json()
    if "error" in metadata:
        raise RuntimeError(metadata["error"])
    (ASSETS / "imagery-georeference.json").write_text(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2))
    image = SESSION.get(metadata["href"], timeout=120)
    image.raise_for_status()
    (ASSETS / "source-aerial.jpg").write_bytes(image.content)
    source = np.array(Image.open(ASSETS / "source-aerial.jpg"))
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:2048, 0:2048]
    mx, my = mercator.transform(BOUNDS[0] + (xx + .5) * 1600 / 2048,
                               BOUNDS[3] - (yy + .5) * 1600 / 2048)
    extent = metadata["extent"]
    u = (mx - extent["xmin"]) / (extent["xmax"] - extent["xmin"]) * source.shape[1] - .5
    v = (extent["ymax"] - my) / (extent["ymax"] - extent["ymin"]) * source.shape[0] - .5
    rectified = np.stack([map_coordinates(source[:, :, c], [v, u], order=1, mode="nearest")
                          for c in range(3)], axis=-1)
    Image.fromarray(rectified).save(ASSETS / "dublin-aerial.jpg", quality=97)
    with Image.open(ASSETS / "dublin-aerial.jpg") as im:
        im.resize((1024, 1024)).save(ASSETS / "aerial-preview.jpg")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    fetch_sources()
```
